note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Main concern: Progressive numbness/tingling and perceived weakness in the left arm/hand.
  - Possible trigger: Began after starting a boxing class a few weeks ago. Patient initially typed “jaw pain,” but states this is not the primary issue.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Tingling began ~2 weeks ago, progressed to numbness extending from elbow into hand.
  - Current symptoms include palmar numbness/tingling affecting digits 2–4; present at rest.
  - Intermittent left shoulder pain with certain movements.
  - Tried massage and warm baths without improvement; ibuprofen taken for right-hand knuckle pain (boxing-related), not helpful for numbness.
  - Transient visual disturbance: “couldn’t see” part of the field in the left eye, lasting ~20 minutes a few weeks ago, resolved.
  - Recent significant viral-like illness ~1 month ago lasting ~2 weeks.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Not discussed/reported in transcript. Jaw pain was mentioned only as an initial typed complaint; no further details provided.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - No prior similar neurologic episodes reported apart from the single transient visual disturbance.
  - No ED visits/hospitalizations or injection therapies reported.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: Not discussed.
  - Medications:
    - Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) for right-hand knuckle pain.
    - Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Iron supplement recommended by PCP; patient often forgets to take (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Participating in a new boxing class for several weeks.
  - Right-hand dominant; notes fine motor difficulty on piano with the left hand.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - Not stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - Not stated.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - No seizures or loss of consciousness reported. Other features not recorded.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected neurologic etiology requiring urgent evaluation; demyelinating disease such as multiple sclerosis considered by clinician given transient left-eye visual field loss (~20 minutes) and progressive left arm paresthesia/weakness over ~2 weeks. Recent viral illness noted. Boxing-related injury considered less likely by clinician.
- No ENT airway or otologic complaints elicited in this consult.
- Conflict noted: Patient initially answered “Yes, absolutely” to neck pain, then immediately stated “No… nothing.”

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Urgent neurology referral arranged by clinician; likely to include brain imaging.
  - No medications initiated at this stage. Clinician noted steroids can be used for acute episodes of suspected MS but requires confirmed diagnosis first.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - While awaiting neurology assessment, monitor for progression or new symptoms.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - “If the weakness progresses to your legs, or there’s any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E.”
- Follow-up:
  - Await urgent neurology appointment and investigations.
  - No ENT-specific follow-up arranged in this consult.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements for an acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  - Allergy list not documented.
  - Comprehensive ENT review of systems (throat tightness, voice changes, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, dyspnea/stridor, nasal/ear symptoms) not elicited.
  - ENT/airway examination and cranial nerve exam not performed/documented.
  - Vitals not recorded.
  - Past ENT history (e.g., sinus/ear disorders, TMJ specifics for jaw pain) not obtained.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Neck pain: patient said “Yes” then immediately “No” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear. Telehealth context with some filler words and minor interruptions; no major audio issues noted.
